method: Read all 14 assigned incoming sources in full from preserved HTML, and checked XML date attributes and people, excluded text, footnotes, apparatus, scholarly siblings, bibliographies and available figures. Compared source-indicated references backward against the assigned Darwin target set only; retained likely responses to unassigned Darwin letters as holds rather than inventing edges. Mixed authorship, public/institutional status, enclosure custody and source date bounds are recorded per source.

incoming_reviews.title: From C. L. Hughes 2 November 1832
incoming_reviews.summary: Hughes provides a detailed river and overland route from Colonia to Mercedes, with costs, landmarks, wildlife, lodging and practical warnings. It is logistical advice for a Darwin journey, but no assigned Darwin letter names this request.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Sarah Williams 21 October 1833
incoming_reviews.summary: Sarah reports family health, domestic news and private confidences, repeatedly recalling Darwin and asking him to write. It is a family letter with no scientific prompt and no identified target in this packet.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Fanny Myddelton Biddulph [c. 21 October 1833]
incoming_reviews.summary: Biddulph adds family health, marriages, children and local news to a packet being sent by Catherine. The voice is hers and explicitly says she has seen little of Darwin’s letters; it cannot be merged with Sarah Williams’s letter.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From T. C. Eyton 12 November 1833
incoming_reviews.summary: Eyton reports Hope’s illness, his own bird anatomy and collections, current ornithological publications and advice on preserving skins. He learned Darwin’s address from Darwin’s sister and mentions Hope, but the body does not identify which Darwin letter supplied the prompt.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From R. E. Alison [March – July 1835]
incoming_reviews.summary: This short memorandum records Valparaiso sea-wall and harbour-depth testimony from older residents, including 1680–1820 changes, and is signed by Alison. It is observational evidence likely accompanying an unassigned Darwin inquiry, with a broad composite date.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From R. E. Alison 25 June 1835
incoming_reviews.summary: Alison explicitly acknowledges Darwin’s 29 May letter and reports raised shell beds, fossils, shoreline perforations, earthquake evidence and uncertainty about uplift, sending specimens. It answers a Darwin geological inquiry whose assigned target is absent; the June date must not be substituted for later Darwin geological letters.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Thomas Sutcliffe [28 August – 5 September 1834]
incoming_reviews.summary: Sutcliffe supplies a rough route croquis from Santiago through Calera, Rancagua and Tagua Tagua, with estates, roads and letters of introduction. The map has two preserved image elements and is practical travel guidance, not a response identifiable to an assigned target.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: 2 inline figure element(s) checked in body HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From F. A. Eck [before 13 October 1834]
incoming_reviews.summary: Eck’s compact table lists barometric elevations for named Chilean places from Great Bell Mountain to Quebrada Verde. It is a numerical memorandum with a pre-13 October bound and no surviving cover prompt in this scope.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Charles D. Douglas 24 February 1835
incoming_reviews.summary: Douglas sends beetles from Chiloé and a tightly dated earthquake observation, then records granite blocks, a possible future survey and forwarding through Robert Burr. The source combines specimen custody with field observations and an open future report.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From C. D. Douglas 5 January 1836
incoming_reviews.summary: Douglas says he received Darwin’s July letter and has investigated its questions, then supplies extensive earthquake, volcano, tide and weather observations from notes and oral reports. The source itself separates reported information from his notebook observations and preserves many dated subsections; the named July prompt is not assigned here.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From R. H. Corfield 26–7 June 1835
incoming_reviews.summary: Corfield acknowledges Darwin’s arrival at Coquimbo, promises to forward letters, accounts for laundry and cash, and adds a dated June 27 postscript with shipping and social news. Receipt, forwarding and later postscript sections are distinct.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From R. H. Corfield 14 — 18 July 1835
incoming_reviews.summary: Corfield sends papers and shipping news, discusses whether he will return to England or enter a long partnership, and adds a July 18 continuation about the Tory ministry and Alison’s requested newspaper. The source says he has not read the enclosed papers, so enclosure availability is not reading evidence.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Charles San Lambert [c. July 1835]
incoming_reviews.summary: The first three paragraphs are San Lambert’s rough sulphur-route memorandum, with visible raw corruption; P4 explicitly marks the following as Darwin’s extract and note. The final text therefore cannot be treated as a single-author incoming letter or as clean Darwin prose.

authority.label: Charles San Lambert, with Charles Darwin extract/note

incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

incoming_reviews.title: From Charles Lyell 26 December 1836
incoming_reviews.summary: Lyell has read Darwin’s paper, invites him to review marked passages, discusses uplift of the Pampas and Andes, fossil-shell comparison and official scientific duties, and arranges a dinner. This is a response to Darwin’s paper, but no assigned target in this group is that paper.
incoming_reviews.figure_note: No inline figure was present in the preserved HTML.

findings: DCP-LETT-277 explicitly answers a Darwin letter dated 29 May and DCP-LETT-292 explicitly answers a Darwin letter dated 27 July, but neither prompt is among the assigned targets; both are retained as source-specific unassigned-prompt holds.

DCP-LETT-228 learned Darwin’s address from his sister and discusses Hope, but does not identify a Darwin letter or distinctive prompt. DCP-LETT-220 and 221 are separate family voices in the same packet and do not supply one another’s missing prompts.

DCP-LETT-255, 256, 269 and 279 contain practical or scientific material with composite dates, copied/extracted sections or raw damage; topic overlap with Darwin geology targets is insufficient for a link.
DCP-LETT-278 and 280 contain receipt, forwarding, and later dated additions; the statement that papers were sent or not read does not prove Darwin’s access to their contents.
DCP-LETT-335 responds to Darwin’s paper, but no assigned target in this packet is that paper; Lyell’s scientific discussion is not reassigned to the fossil-offer or public-letter records.
limitations: No unassigned Darwin target was synthesized. Broad or approximate source dates remain bounded as recorded. Inline figures were inspected for availability; no visual was used as evidence for a relationship.

source_evidence.quote: By the arrival of the Beagle on the 14th. Inst. I recd. your much esteemed letter of the 29th. May
source_evidence.interpretation: Explicitly identifies a Darwin prompt dated 29 May; the corresponding Darwin source is outside this assigned target set.

source_evidence.quote: I recieved your kind letter on the 27th. of July last year
source_evidence.interpretation: Explicitly identifies a Darwin prompt dated 27 July; this does not establish a link to a later assigned target.

source_evidence.quote: I have read your paper1 with the greatest pleasure
source_evidence.interpretation: Confirms Lyell read a Darwin paper; the paper is not identified as an assigned target in this group.
